name: Adam
summary: The first human, formed from the dust of the ground and placed in the Garden of Eden to tend it. His disobedience with Eve, eating the forbidden fruit, brought sin and death into the world.

name: Eve
summary: The first woman, formed from Adam's rib and called 'the mother of all living.' Deceived by the serpent, she ate the forbidden fruit and shared it with Adam.

name: Cain
summary: Adam and Eve's firstborn, a farmer. When his offering was not accepted and his brother's was, he killed Abel in the field, and was sent out as a wanderer under God's protective mark.

name: Abel
summary: Adam and Eve's second son, a shepherd. He brought the firstborn of his flock and God accepted it — and his brother killed him for it.

name: Noah
summary: A righteous man in a corrupt generation, instructed by God to build an ark to save his family and pairs of every animal from a great flood.

name: Abraham
summary: Called by God to leave his homeland for a land he would be shown, and promised he would become the father of a great nation. Originally named Abram.

name: Sarah
summary: Abraham's wife, who remained childless into old age until God fulfilled his promise and she gave birth to Isaac. Originally named Sarai.

name: Hagar
summary: Sarah's Egyptian servant, given to Abraham to bear a child. Mistreated and twice driven into the wilderness, she is the only person in Genesis to give God a name: the God who sees me.

name: Lot
summary: Abraham's nephew, who left Haran with him. Given first choice of the land he took the well-watered Jordan valley, settled toward Sodom, and had to be pulled out of it by angels.

name: Ishmael
summary: Abraham's firstborn, born to Hagar, Sarah's Egyptian servant. Sent away with his mother after Isaac was born, but God promised to make him into a great nation as well.

name: Isaac
summary: The long-promised son of Abraham and Sarah. As a young man he was offered by Abraham as a sacrifice in a test of faith, then spared by God's provision of a ram.

name: Rebekah
summary: Isaac's wife, chosen at a well by Abraham's servant. Mother of twins Jacob and Esau, she favored Jacob and helped him secure his father's blessing.

name: Esau
summary: Isaac and Rebekah's elder twin, a skilled hunter who sold his birthright to Jacob for a bowl of stew and was later denied their father's primary blessing.

name: Jacob
summary: Isaac and Rebekah's younger twin, who obtained his brother Esau's birthright and blessing. Later renamed Israel after wrestling with God, he fathered twelve sons who became the twelve tribes of Israel.

name: Rachel
summary: The younger daughter of Laban, whom Jacob loved and worked fourteen years for. Barren for years while her sister bore sons, she became the mother of Joseph and died bearing Benjamin.

name: Leah
summary: Laban's elder daughter, given to Jacob in place of Rachel. Unloved but not unseen — God opened her womb, and her fourth son Judah became the line of the kings.

name: Joseph
summary: Jacob's favored son, sold into slavery in Egypt by his jealous brothers. Rose to become second-in-command to Pharaoh, and later saved his family from famine.

name: Moses
summary: Born under a death sentence and hidden in a basket on the Nile, raised in Pharaoh's own household, and forty years later called by name out of a bush that would not burn out. He would lead Israel out of Egypt.

name: Jochebed
roles: hid her son in defiance of Pharaoh
mother of Moses, Aaron and Miriam
summary: A Hebrew woman who hid her infant son three months, then risked the river rather than Pharaoh's decree — and was hired, without Pharaoh's daughter ever knowing who she was, to nurse her own child.

name: Miriam
summary: Moses' older sister, who watched from a distance as the basket drifted, then stepped forward with exactly the right question to put her own mother at her brother's side.

name: Aaron
summary: Moses' elder brother, sent by God into the wilderness to meet him and become the voice of a man who called himself slow of speech.

name: Pharaoh's Daughter
summary: An Egyptian princess who found a Hebrew baby in the reeds, had compassion on him despite knowing exactly who he was, and raised her own people's intended victim in the palace itself.

name: Zipporah
roles: met at a well in Midian
summary: A priest of Midian's daughter, one of seven sisters Moses defended at a well. She became his wife during his forty years in exile, and bore him a son.

name: Naomi
roles: lost everything, then found fullness again
summary: Widowed and left childless in Moab, she returned to Bethlehem calling herself Mara — bitter — and left it again a grandmother, in the family line of David.

name: Ruth
roles: stayed when she could have gone home
summary: A Moabite widow who refused to leave her mother-in-law, gleaned in a stranger's field to keep them both alive, and asked for redemption rather than charity. Her line runs to David, and further.

name: Boaz
summary: A prosperous relative of Naomi's dead husband, who noticed a foreign gleaner in his field, protected her, and redeemed her family's inheritance and her future when a nearer relative would not.

name: Elimelech
summary: Naomi's husband, who took his family from Bethlehem to Moab to escape a famine, and died there before ever seeing them return.

name: Orpah
summary: Naomi's other daughter-in-law, who loved her enough to weep at their parting, but chose — reasonably, and without condemnation in the text — to return to her own people and gods rather than follow her into an uncertain future.

name: Pharaoh
roles: let Egypt's firstborn die rather than let Israel go
summary: The king of Egypt who enslaved Israel and refused, plague after plague, to let them go. The text never gives him a name — he represents the throne more than a single ruler across the narrative.

name: Joshua
roles: wouldn't leave the Tent of Meeting
summary: Moses' young aide, first seen leading Israel's fighting men against Amalek and lingering in the tent of meeting after Moses left it. He becomes the far more central figure who leads Israel into the promised land.

name: Nadab
summary: Aaron's oldest son, ordained a priest alongside his father and brothers — and killed by fire from Yahweh days later for offering incense God never commanded.

name: Abihu
summary: Aaron's second son, ordained alongside his brother Nadab and killed with him the same way, in the same moment.

name: Caleb
roles: believed they could take the land
summary: One of the twelve spies sent into Canaan, and one of only two who came back saying Israel could take it. For that, he was the only man of his generation, besides Joshua, who lived to enter the land.

name: Korah
summary: A Levite who led an open challenge to Moses and Aaron's authority, claiming the whole congregation was equally holy. The ground opened beneath him, his fellow rebels, and their households.

name: Eleazar
summary: Aaron's son, given his father's priestly garments on Mount Hor the day Aaron died. He carries the priesthood forward into the next generation.

name: Balaam
summary: A foreign prophet hired by a Moabite king to curse Israel. His own donkey saw the angel blocking the road before he did — and when he finally spoke over Israel, blessing came out instead of the curse he was paid for.

name: Rahab
roles: chose Israel's God over her own people
summary: A woman of Jericho who hid two Israelite spies on her roof, believing Yahweh had already given them the land. She and her family were the only ones spared when the city fell.

name: Achan
summary: A man of Judah who secretly took silver, gold, and a robe from Jericho's forbidden plunder. Israel was routed at Ai until he was found out and stoned.
